name_en: Maynard's theorem on small gaps between primes
canonical_name: Maynard small-prime-gaps and bounded-prime-clusters theorem family
literal_source_claim_en: Improvement of the upper bound on prime gaps.
statement_blocker: The catalog gives only an attribution, year, and qualitative improvement gloss. Maynard's matching paper has inequivalent Theorems 1.1-1.4 and a separate sieve engine: general m-step bounds, tuple-density, an unconditional adjacent-gap bound of 600, and conditional Elliott-Halberstam bounds. The catalog fixes neither result, constant, gap notion, quantifiers, conditionality, source edition, nor indexing and liminf encoding. Selecting one proposition at intake would invent or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: the approved source must fix positive versus zero-based naturals, one-based versus zero-based nth-prime indexing, the gap codomain and subtraction, finite-set and tuple encodings if relevant, real/asymptotic structures, filter and liminf conventions, and all universe and coercion choices.
conclusion: Open: one approved result from the source family, such as the unconditional general m-step bound, the unconditional adjacent-gap bound 600, a positive-proportion tuple theorem, or an explicitly conditional level-of-distribution conclusion; no one result is selected.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; statement freeze must resolve all indexing, m=0, finite-prefix, equality, subtraction, asymptotic-constant, tuple-cardinality, and conditional-boundary cases listed in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: Maynard, Small gaps between primes, Theorem 1.1: for positive m, liminf of p_(n+m)-p_n is bounded by an absolute constant times m^3 exp(4m)
Maynard, Small gaps between primes, Theorem 1.2: a positive proportion of m-subsets in any sufficiently large finite set are prime tuples in the stated infinitude sense
Maynard, Small gaps between primes, Theorem 1.3: unconditionally liminf of adjacent prime gaps is at most 600
Maynard, Small gaps between primes, Theorem 1.4: under full level of distribution, adjacent and two-step liminf bounds 12 and 600
Maynard, Small gaps between primes, Propositions 4.2-4.3: the multidimensional sieve and variational criterion behind the headline consequences
the abstract's weaker finite-liminf consequence for every positive m
